description: Adopts the same deliberate Renovate config already committed byte-for-byte to the
other four 'ecosystem bridge' orbs (bitrise, harness, bitbucket-pipes, buildkite) --
cci-labs/act was excluded from that earlier rollout only because it was mid-flight on
this own upgrade branch; this file brings it into line now that the branch is landing.
Every non-default setting below carries its own "description" explaining why it
departs from config:recommended. Two things this config will NEVER do, by design:
(1) touch git tags, and (2) auto-merge anything -- this orb is consumed by customers,
and its own release-filters (tag regex /^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$/) gates a real
production orb publish (orb-tools/publish, pub_type: production). Renovate only ever
opens branches/PRs against a normal base branch and has no mechanism to push a tag on
its own, so this risk is structural, not just configured away -- but automerge is
disabled twice below (automerge + platformAutomerge) as defense in depth anyway.
Pinning vs. ranging: CircleCI orb references (namespace/orb@X.Y.Z) have no range syntax
at all -- every reference is already a single exact version, enforced by the platform.
Since this orb is itself published for customers to depend on, treating our own
upstream pins (circleci/orb-tools, circleci/shellcheck) the same way -- one reviewed,
revertible commit per bump -- gives a clean paper trail from 'a production publish went
bad' back to 'this exact tooling bump'. We deliberately do NOT move any orb reference to
CircleCI's '@volatile' pseudo-version (always-latest, unpinned) even though Renovate
knows how to skip volatile orbs -- volatile would remove exactly the paper trail pinning
gives us. The same logic extends to Docker: every image already pinned to a real tag
(mvdan/shfmt, redis, android) stays pinned to a real tag and Renovate bumps it like any
other dependency. The only images left unmanaged are CircleCI's own floating 'current'
convenience tags (cimg/base:current in every job's docker executor; ubuntu-2404:current
as the default executor's machine image) -- those are intentionally a moving target
maintained upstream, with no 'newer current' for Renovate to bump to.
Verified against Renovate's own docs before writing this: the circleci manager scans
any file matching /(^|/)\.circleci/.+\.ya?ml$/ and extracts both 'orb' and 'docker'
datasource references from it -- so both .circleci/config.yml and
.circleci/test-deploy.yml are covered with zero extra config. It does NOT reach into
src/**/*.yml (orb source: executors, commands, jobs, examples) -- those either use a
parameterised <<parameters.image>> (nothing concrete to bump, e.g. src/executors/
default.yml's ubuntu-2404:current default) or are illustrative example snippets
(src/examples/*.yml) documenting usage, never executed by this repo's own CI. We
deliberately did not bolt on a custom regex manager to reach into README.md/src/
examples/*.yml: those pins are meant to look like a plausible customer config, not
track upstream, and Renovate silently rewriting a docs example would be a worse outcome
than leaving it alone.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Security-driven bumps should never sit in the queue for a weekly window -- let vulnerability-alert PRs raise immediately, on top of (not instead of) the normal weekly schedule everything else uses.

packageRules.description: Group this orb family's own CircleCI orb-tools/shellcheck version bumps into one PR, rather than one PR per orb -- an orb-tools bump changes the same lint/pack/review/continue pipeline every one of these repos shares, so reviewing them together (and running the one shared CI matrix once) is more useful than reviewing them apart.

Group every OTHER Docker image actually pinned to a real, resolvable tag -- .circleci/config.yml's shfmt-check image (mvdan/shfmt), and .circleci/test-deploy.yml's pinned test-fixture images (redis, android) -- into one PR per digest/tag-bump cycle instead of a flood of one-image-at-a-time PRs. These are all test/tooling images with zero customer-facing blast radius, so grouping for review convenience costs nothing.
packageRules.groupName: docker image tag/digest updates (test + tooling images)

packageRules.description: Do NOT try to bump CircleCI's own floating 'current' convenience tags (cimg/base:current in check-cli-version and every test-deploy docker job; ubuntu-2404:current as the machine-executor default). 'current' is maintained and moved forward by CircleCI itself, on purpose, as the whole point of using it instead of a dated tag -- there is no 'newer current' for Renovate to open a PR for, and treating it as a version to pin would fight the reason these jobs use 'current' in the first place.

Do NOT try to resolve or bump ':local' image tags -- carried over from the shared config for consistency even though this repo has none today (no image here is built ad hoc inside a test job and left unpushed). Kept so a future test fixture that does introduce one doesn't generate lookup-failure noise on the Dependency Dashboard.
